title: Observer’s guide for ISO 2026-W18
planetary_coordinate: geocentric tropical ecliptic longitude; Monday 00:00 UTC

planet_relations.basis: Star Almanack preserved geocentric tropical ecliptic longitude

note:
ISO 2026-W18 runs from April 27 through May 3. Venus and Uranus are separated by about 3.4° in geocentric ecliptic longitude at the Monday 00:00 UTC snapshot.

**Naked eye:** 🌕 Full Moon · Milk Moon — 17:23:11 UTC. Bright moonlight favors prominent stars and planets while reducing contrast on faint deep-sky objects. No fixed-sky Calendar object is classified for naked-eye observing this week.

**Planets:** Venus and Uranus are separated by about 3.4° in geocentric ecliptic longitude at the Monday 00:00 UTC snapshot.

**Binoculars:** No fixed-sky Calendar object is classified for binocular observing this week.

**Small telescope:** Concentrate on M65, M66. Increase magnification only after the target and surrounding pattern are secure.

**Substantial telescope:** No fixed-sky Calendar object is classified as requiring a substantial telescope this week.

descriptors.name: Full Moon
descriptors.summary: One lunar event with both its astronomical phase and seasonal designation.
descriptors.body: Full Moon is the lunar phase in which the Moon and Sun are approximately opposite in geocentric ecliptic longitude, so the lunar disk is fully illuminated as seen from Earth.
